caption: Blur: sparks that spread into soft clouds as last frame's picture is blurred under them
why: A sharp dot on a few dozen LEDs looks harsh; light in the real world spreads. Blur reads last frame's picture, softened - each pixel the average of the ones around it - so whatever you blend it with has a soft spread of its past around it.

Fed back into the picture through a Fade it makes things bloom and drift into clouds; added lightly it is a soft halo. Its neighbours: Glow does the bloom in one node; Previous is last frame unblurred; Blur is last frame, softened.
steps: Blur has no inputs: it reads the whole of last frame's picture. **radius** is 1: each pixel is the average of the 3 x 3 around it.
A **Fade** (keep 0.94) dims the blurred picture a little each frame, so old light dies away.
New light: a **Sparkle** (density 0.02, reseeded eight times a second) lights a few pixels in the **Palette**'s colour for their place.

A **Blend** in max mode keeps the brighter of the fading blur and the new sparks; the result is the **Output** - and next frame's Blur reads it, so every spark spreads out a pixel further each frame and fades as it goes.

try.label: Wider spread
try.text: radius 2: each frame averages the 5 x 5 around, so the clouds spread twice as fast.

try.label: Linger
try.text: the Fade's keep at 0.985: the light dies slowly, so the clouds build up and merge.

try.label: No feedback
try.text: the Fade's keep at 0: the blur is gone each frame, leaving the sparks sharp and alone - Blur only does anything by reading what came before.
